finding.claim: The authenticated identity is read directly from a client-controllable HTTP header with no verification in the application. Any caller who can reach the app without a trusting proxy that strips and overwrites this header can impersonate any user named in a resource's grants and pass every ACL check. The header name suggests an upstream proxy sets it, so this depends on deployment. The app does not enforce that precondition.
finding.source: Request header X-Session-User-Verified, supplied by the remote client
finding.sink: ensure_allowed/is_allowed authorization for DELETE /files/<fid> (views.py:17) and POST /files/<fid>/rename (views.py:25), which then run del STORE[fid] and f['name'] = ...

trace.note: g.user = request.headers.get('X-Session-User-Verified') with no signature, session, or proxy check
is_allowed only checks that the claimed user string appears in resource grants
the file is deleted once the spoofed user passes the check
rename_file uses the same spoofed identity and then writes the name at line 27

finding.guards_checked: Checked ensure_allowed (aborts with 403 on denial) and is_allowed (its result is used and returned as 403 in rename_file). A missing header gives g.user=None, which has no grants and is denied. No authentication or token verification and no stripping of the header exists in the code. Unauthorized-method and IDOR checks were fine: both routes authorize against the fetched object. Lower-severity issues not reported as separate findings: STORE[fid] raises KeyError for unknown ids, giving a 500 instead of a 404, and request.json['name'] is unvalidated.

verdict.guard_found: ensure_allowed (acl.py:8-10, aborts 403) and is_allowed (acl.py:4-5, result tested at views.py:25) only check the claimed user string against the resource's grants. No code authenticates or strips the header.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (views.py:11 trusts the X-Session-User-Verified header, views.py:17/25 authorize on it, views.py:18/27 are the effects, and acl.py:5 only checks the string against grants). Whether a client can spoof it depends on whether a header-stripping proxy sits in front of the app, which the repo, containing only views.py and acl.py, does not show.
